posts.headline: Bitcoin has slid to around $61,600 — roughly half its October 2025 peak — and if you own any, directly or through an ETF, that drop is yours.
posts.source: Source: The Motley Fool / Crypto Briefing, Nov. 19, 2026
posts.caption:
Bitcoin just slid to around $61,600 — and if you own any, or hold a Bitcoin ETF in your brokerage or retirement account, this drop is yours.

It traded near $61,635 on the evening of Nov. 19, down about 13% on the week and closing in on $60,000 (The Motley Fool). That's roughly half its October 2025 peak near $126,000, and a sixth straight losing week (Crypto Briefing).

US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen more than $2.5 billion pulled out in 2026, per CoinDesk, as the Fed signals higher rates for longer.

My take: 'it's in my 401(k) now' cuts both ways — the same door that let the gains in lets a near-50% drop in too.

Own any Bitcoin, in the US or Canada — are you holding or trimming?

paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $61,635 on the evening of Nov. 19, down about 2% on the day and roughly 13% over the week, closing in on the $60,000 line. (The Motley Fool / FMP, Nov. 19)
It peaked near $126,000 in October 2025, so the price is now close to half what it was — a month-to-date fall of roughly 16% to 23%, and a sixth straight losing week. (Crypto Briefing)

Why it's your money: Bitcoin now sits in brokerage accounts and some retirement plans via spot ETFs — which have shed over $2.5 billion in 2026, per CoinDesk. The new worry: a Fed signalling higher rates, not cuts.
